VP, Revenue (Remote) in San Francisco at Monks | Apply now! – Vaia – Talents

# VP, Revenue (Remote) in San Francisco 

 San Francisco Full-Time Remote 

### At a Glance

- Tasks: Lead revenue growth and optimize commercial performance in a dynamic media environment.
- Company: Join Monks, a global leader in digital marketing and technology services.
- Benefits: Enjoy full medical coverage, generous PTO, 401k contributions, and a focus on work-life balance.
- Other info: Be part of a diverse culture committed to equity, inclusion, and sustainable growth.
- Why this job: Make a real impact in a fast-paced, innovative company with entrepreneurial opportunities.
- Qualifications: 10+ years in revenue leadership roles with strong sales and operational skills.

Join to apply for the VP, Revenue (Remote) role at Monks. Please do read through the description at least once before clicking on Apply. Please note that we will never request payment or bank account information at any stage of the recruitment process. As we continue to grow our teams, we urge you to be cautious of fraudulent job postings or recruitment activities that misuse our company name and information. Please protect your personal information during any recruitment process. While Monks may contact potential candidates via LinkedIn, all applications must be submitted through our official website (monks.com/careers).

About The Role

The VP, Revenue is a senior leadership role in the mid-market media business unit responsible for driving revenue growth, optimizing the unit’s commercial performance, and leading the alignment of new business, marketing, and revenue. As a core member of the leadership team, you will be deeply involved in business direction and goal setting, revenue-based decision-making, pipeline health, and innovation in revenue channels. You will collaborate closely with executive leadership to shape our go-to-market approach, lead pricing and profitability decisions, and develop capabilities that position Monks for sustainable growth.

Ideal Candidate

Our ideal candidate is both a commercial strategist and a hands-on leader, combining strong sales acumen, operational rigor, and relentless curiosity about growth levers. You excel at building and coaching high-performing teams, leveraging data to inform executive decisions, and creating a culture centered on client value, market agility, and revenue accountability.

Responsibilities

- Commercial & Strategic Leadership

- Lead business direction, revenue strategy, and goal-setting in collaboration with agency and executive teams.
- Drive oversight of all revenue activities, proactively recommending business and growth priorities, pipeline health, and opportunities for expansion.
- Own forecasting, reporting, and analysis for all revenue channels; adjusting strategies as needed, and partnering on monthly financial reviews.
- Develop and innovate new revenue sources and channels (e.g., partnerships, vendor lists, pitch consultants).
- Align planning and execution across new business, marketing, and revenue operations functions.
- Direct service and capability development based on market trends and agency performance.
- Lead key pricing negotiations, provide profitability guidance, and drive decisions on client upstreaming and pricing changes.
- Business Development & Marketing

- Oversee the new business process alongside a team of sellers: leading pitch qualification, resource coordination, case library and RFP responses, and direct involvement in strategic pitches.
- Responsible for confirming staffing, pricing, and planning for new account wins.
- Collaborate with team leaders to ensure accurate new client resourcing and pipeline tracking.
- Oversee and align the marketing department’s work with revenue objectives, brand positioning, and ICP (Ideal Customer Profile) strategy.
- Set marketing goals and KPIs, ensuring marketing initiatives drive measurable impact on revenue and brand value.
- Maintain a best-in-class enablement suite: pitch decks, sales tools, product demos, and strategic documentation.
- Client Growth & Retention

- Oversee and coach on renewals, cross-sells, and pricing strategies for existing clients to drive retention and expansion.
- Direct involvement in high-stakes renewal and procurement conversations.
- Build and reinforce a culture of revenue contribution and commercial acumen within the accounts team.
- Proactively manage and track revenue opportunities, forecasts, and client context to maximize renewals and upsell rates.
- Team Leadership & Operations

- Directly manage leaders in marketing and new business.
- Coach and develop direct reports, oversee PRs, and drive clarity in team roles, hiring, and bandwidth needs.
- Strategically allocate resources across programs that most directly influence revenue growth and team efficiency.
- Routinely review contracts at a high level of attention to detail.
- Drive continuous improvement in processes, technology, and reporting throughout the revenue cycle.

Qualifications

- 10+ years in revenue-focused leadership roles across business development, marketing, sales operations, or revenue operations, ideally in agency or media environments.
- Experience in setting business strategy, leading forecasting, and managing P&L for agency or high-growth commercial businesses.
- Proven leadership in developing high-performing teams in marketing, sales, or revenue operations functions.
- Demonstrated ability to innovate new revenue channels, own complex negotiations, and influence executive decision-makers.
- Advanced skills in commercial analytics, revenue reporting, pipeline management, and CRM or revenue operations tooling.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including c-suite and board-level engagement.

Equal Opportunity Statement

At Monks, we believe in fostering an environment where a diversity of perspectives can thrive. We proactively work to design hiring processes that promote equity and inclusion while mitigating bias. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building a team that reflects the communities we serve. We welcome and encourage qualified applicants, from all backgrounds, who are excited to contribute to our mission.

Benefits

- Excellent, full coverage medical, dental, and vision insurance.
- Generous PTO and 15 company-wide holidays.
- 401k with company contribution.
- Paid parental leave.
- Work-life balance with an emphasis on personal well-being.
- Career growth in a disruptor space & entrepreneurial opportunities within the Monks network.
- A globally diverse & inclusive culture with employee resource groups such as S4 Melanin, Pride.Monks, Cultura.Monks, and more!
- Authentic commitment to DEI efforts and sustainable growth.

This role is subject to our Return to Office (RTO) policy. If you reside within a commutable distance of one of our office locations, you will be expected to work from the office a set number of days per week. The specific details, including the number of required office days, will be in accordance with the company’s then-current RTO policy, which is subject to change from time to time.

Monks has provided a compensation range that represents its good faith estimate of what Monks may pay for the position at the time of posting. Monks may ultimately pay more or less than the posted compensation range. The salary offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on job-related factors, but not based on a candidate’s sex or any other protected status.

Monks is the global, purely digital, unitary operating brand of S4Capital plc. With a legacy of innovation and specialized expertise, Monks combines an extraordinary range of global marketing and technology services to accelerate business possibilities and redefine how brands and businesses interact with the world.

### VP, Revenue (Remote) in San Francisco employer: Monks

At Monks, we pride ourselves on being an exceptional employer that values diversity, collaboration, and professional growth. Our remote/hybrid work culture allows for flexibility while fostering strong team dynamics and mentorship opportunities, ensuring that every employee can thrive in their role. With a commitment to equity and inclusion, we empower our team members to take ownership of their projects and contribute meaningfully to our clients' success.

Contact Detail:

Monks Recruiting Team

### Vaia Expert Advice🤫

We think this is how you could land VP, Revenue (Remote) in San Francisco

✨ Tip Number 1

Network like a pro! Reach out to your connections on LinkedIn and let them know you're on the hunt for a VP, Revenue role. You never know who might have the inside scoop on opportunities or can refer you directly.

✨ Tip Number 2

Prepare for interviews by practicing your pitch. Highlight your experience in driving revenue growth and leading teams. Make sure to showcase your strategic thinking and how you've innovated in past roles.

✨ Tip Number 3

Stay updated on industry trends! Being knowledgeable about the latest in media and revenue strategies will not only impress interviewers but also help you align your vision with Monks' goals.

✨ Tip Number 4

Don't forget to apply through our website! It's the best way to ensure your application gets seen. Plus, it shows you're serious about joining the Monks team!

#### We think you need these skills to ace VP, Revenue (Remote) in San Francisco

Data-Driven Decision Making

Client Relationship Management

Commercial Analytics

Showcase Your Experience: When writing your application, make sure to highlight your relevant experience in revenue-focused leadership roles. We want to see how your background aligns with our needs, so don’t hold back on those impressive achievements!

Be Authentic: Let your personality shine through in your application! We value authenticity and want to get a sense of who you are beyond just your qualifications. Share your passion for growth and innovation in the revenue space.

Apply Through Our Website: Remember, all applications must be submitted through our official website. This helps us keep everything organized and ensures your application gets the attention it deserves. So, head over to monks.com/careers and let’s get started!

### How to prepare for a job interview at Monks

✨ Know Your Numbers

As a VP of Revenue, you'll need to demonstrate your understanding of revenue metrics and forecasting. Brush up on key performance indicators relevant to the role, like pipeline health and profitability. Be ready to discuss how you've used data to drive decisions in past roles.

✨ Showcase Your Leadership Style

This position requires strong leadership skills, so be prepared to share examples of how you've built and coached high-performing teams. Talk about your approach to team dynamics and how you foster a culture of accountability and growth within your teams.

✨ Align with Company Goals

Research Monks' mission and values, and think about how your vision aligns with theirs. Be ready to discuss how you can contribute to their growth strategy and what innovative revenue channels you might explore to help them achieve their objectives.

✨ Prepare for Strategic Conversations

Expect to engage in discussions about pricing strategies and client negotiations. Prepare examples of complex negotiations you've led and the outcomes. Highlight your ability to influence executive decision-makers and how you approach high-stakes conversations.

### Bosch tests Monk.AI image analysis technology in evaluating vehicle damages

Bosch, together with French startup, Monk.AI are piloting technology to be used in the evaluation of vehicle damages. Bosch regularly seeks out partners to enrich service offerings for customers and the goal of this collaboration is to explore how Monk’s image analysis technology could contribute to solving damage detection tasks. The team has been testing the algorithm performances in challenging environments and for various use cases such as in optimizing fleets and workshops operations. One of the highlights of the technology is that it works on any conventional camera, including smartphones.

# The GTMnow Podcast

GTMnow

The GTMnow Podcast interviews well-known tech executive, VC, and founders - the expert operators in the trenches who have ‘been there, done that’ to build some of the fastest-growing software companies. Every week, a guest joins Sophie Buonassisi to dissect their stories, revealing expert insights around what worked, what didn’t, and how things actually went down. This podcast is produced by GTMnow, the media brand of GTMfund - sharing insight on go-to-market from working with hundreds of portfolio companies backed by over 350 of the best go-to-market executives. GTMfund is an early-stage VC fund focused on investing in the most exciting, up-and-coming B2B SaaS companies across the world. The LP network consists of VP and C-level Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success leaders from companies like DocuSign, Salesforce, LinkedIn, Snowflake, Okta, Zoom, and many more. Visit gtmnow.com for more details and to sign up for our newsletter and other content resources.

## Episodes 

1. 1d ago 

 The ex-engineer who says sales beats product | George Kurdin (CEO, Monk) 

 George was a professional poker player, then CEO of a company that sold to Logitech for around $100M, and now he’s the CEO of Monk, an AI company automating accounts receivable. Monk is an API company solving the other side of the ledger from Ramp: getting B2B invoices paid. George gets candid about the go-to-market mistakes he made (“50 more than I expected”), why vertical companies win on in-person workshops, the proprietary “harness” that he argues is the real moat in applied AI, the extreme-accountability culture he runs with 16 people and almost no meetings, and his sharpest tactical advice on fundraising, websites, and co-founder relationships. Brought to you by: Nooks - discover how revenue agents can transform your GTM at https://nooks.ai/gtmfund Transcript: Full interview transcripts can be found by episode at https://gtmnow.com/tag/podcast/ What you’ll learn: - Why sales and marketing is “tier zero,” and why he used to believe the opposite (“if you build it, they will come” is wrong) - Two lessons from pro poker that transfer to building: stay disciplined through variance, and adapt or get destroyed - Why go-to-market has never been more nuanced, and why vertical companies are winning with in-person workshops and lunch-and-learns over cold email - The pre-seed website bet: why spending big on a cohesive visual identity early lifted one company’s close rate ~50% - The “harness” thesis: why owning your own evals, guardrails, and tests (not just calling the models) is the moat in applied AI - How to run extreme accountability: everything in Slack, blameless retros, almost no meetings, 16 people - Why they reverse-engineered into a huge-TAM problem on purpose (recruiting, and not getting disrupted by the frontier labs) - Why hard ROI (dollars in your pocket) now beats “time savings” as an AI value prop - Fundraising: compress the process to create FOMO, and why how you run the raise signals how you run the company - Why the co-founder relationship matters more than the idea, and how to invest in it like a marriage George, Co-Founder and CEO at Monk LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/georgekurdin Monk: https://monk.com/ Sophie Buonassisi: LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sophiebuonassisi/ X: https://x.com/sophiebuona About the guest: George is the co-founder and CEO of Monk, an API company that automates accounts receivable (collections and cash application) for B2B businesses using AI. He was previously CEO of Streamlabs, which sold to Logitech (reported around $100M) in 2019, and before his operating career he was a professional poker player for about five years. Monk is based in New York and has raised roughly $28M, including a Series A. His co-founder is Joe. About GTMnow: GTMnow is the media arm of GTMfund, sharing the strategies, tactics, and stories from the operators and investors building the next generation of go-to-market. Conversations reveal the unshared details behind how they have grown companies, and the go-to-market strategies responsible for shaping that growth. Visit gtmnow.com for more episodes and other interesting content. 

33m
2. Oct 6 

 Legora's CRO: $3.5M to $200M+ ARR, the Fastest Direct Sales Motion | Patrick Forquer 

 Legora went from $3.5M to over $100M in revenue in about a year, the fastest any company has ever scaled a direct-sales motion from zero to $100M. Then, they doubled revenue in less than 6 months and hit $200M ARR. Patrick spent seven years at Braze, from the early days through IPO, before joining Legora (a vertical legal-AI company founded by Max, backed by Benchmark and Redpoint) at $3.5M in revenue. He shares the scaling journey. He also gets tactical on the three things he looks for before joining a company, why speed-to-value is the number-one leading indicator of revenue performance, the pilot that lets customers keep everything they build even if they walk, how he structures forward-deploy across legal engineers and traditional FDEs, the Jude Law and Aaron Judge campaigns and whether they paid off, the "8 Mile" objection-handling play, and the shift to consumption pricing. He joined at roughly $3.5M in revenue and helped scale it past $100M in about a year, the fastest any company has taken a direct-sales motion from zero to $100M. Now, they’ve hit $200M ARR. Before Legora he spent seven years at Braze, from the early days through its path to IPO. 3. Sep 29 

 Lessons from building 113 AI agents and reinventing a GTM function with AI | Meagan (CMO, Samsara) 

 The CMO of Samsara joins GTMnow to walk through exactly how she ran an AI transformation inside a public company, from a 2.5 week boot camp to 113 agents in production, all while keeping headcount flat and pushing pipeline and revenue up. Meagan has led teams through platform shifts before (PLG, social, Covid) at MongoDB, DocuSign, Nieman, and now Samsara, and she argues AI is categorically different: not a new channel, but a production shift that changes how the work itself gets done. She gets tactical on the change-management sequence (learn by doing before you cap anything), how agents live in Slack for every function, the ABM pages that went from 2-3 weeks to under 30 minutes, the KPIs she tracks, how she interviews for AI fluency, and her message to anxious operators: this is a chance to leapfrog, not a threat. She has led marketing through major platform shifts at MongoDB, DocuSign, and Nieman, and has a background in MIS and computer science, starting her career as an IT engineer before moving into marketing. 4. Sep 23 

 Inside LinkedIn: buyer behavior, how to social sell, why warm intros get 3x the response, why only 45% of sellers are seen as trustworthy and the 4 behaviors that separate top sellers | Catherine Flynn (LinkedIn Sales Navigator) 

 Information has never been more abundant, and trust has never been harder to earn. That's the tension at the heart of LinkedIn's new research, "The Trust Advantage," and Catherine, who leads marketing for LinkedIn's Sales Solutions business (Sales Navigator), joins Sophie Buonassisi on GTMnow to unpack it. The headline gap: 86% of B2B buyers say expertise is what builds trust, but only 45% describe the sellers they meet as trustworthy. Catherine has spent 25+ years in marketing, including 13 at Meta, and now runs a global team out of Singapore. She argues AI has made "spray and pray" easier than ever, which is exactly why the winning move is doing less, more relevant outreach. She breaks down the four behaviors that separate top sellers, why warm introductions convert so much better, what a seller's LinkedIn profile should actually say, and how putting your expertise out publicly now helps both you and your company rank in AI search. What you'll learn: - The trust gap: why 86% of buyers want expertise but only 45% find sellers trustworthy, and how to close it - Why expertise in a first conversation means leading with their problem, not your product - The case for less outreach: more signal means you can be far more selective - The four top-seller behaviors: signal-based selling, early multithreading, timely engagement (hours not weeks), and genuinely personalized outreach - Why warm intros win: ~3x higher email response and ~2x higher connection-acceptance than cold - The most underrated entry point: executive sponsors and former customers who moved companies - What a seller's LinkedIn profile should be (a point of view, not a resume), and why profile views are a top buying signal - The algorithm and discoverability: how posting even once a week, and engaging on others' posts, compounds - Why LinkedIn is now the most-cited domain for professional queries in AI search, and what that means for you - Hiring in the AI era: adaptability and generalists over specialists, and "throw your hat over the wall" Connect with Catherine: LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/catherineflynn/ Host: Sophie Buonassisi, SVP at GTMnow LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sophiebuonassisi/ X: https://x.com/sophiebuona About the guest: Catherine leads marketing for LinkedIn's Sales Solutions business, home of Sales Navigator. She has 25+ years in marketing, including consumer and agency roots and roughly 13 years at Meta/Facebook, and is based in Singapore, where much of the Sales Solutions business is being built across APAC. 42m
5. Sep 15 

 Why More AI Won't Grow Your Revenue (and What Will) | Loreal Lynch (CMO, Nooks) 

 The CMO of Nooks (and former CMO of Jasper) joins GTMnow to explain why buying more agents won't grow revenue unless you rebuild the process underneath, and what the human-plus-agent revenue team truly looks like. Loreal has had a front-row seat to two AI waves: first at Jasper, where AI reshaped marketing content, and now at Nooks, building toward what she calls the revenue agents category. She breaks down why the tools in today's GTM stack were built for humans to click through, not for agents to execute; why the org chart and the process both have to be rethought from the ground up; and why the real shift isn't reps prompting AI, but AI prompting reps. She also gets into the misconception that agents are easy to build, the CMO-CRO alignment model she runs with her counterpart Hannah, and why the marketing pendulum is swinging back from pure performance to brand. What you'll learn: - Why bolting AI tools onto pre-AI processes fails, and what a real revenue operating system requires - The iceberg model of human vs. agent work, and why the waterline keeps rising - Why the future flips: AI stops waiting for prompts and starts prompting the rep - Augmentation over replacement: if an agent makes a rep 10x, you hire more reps, not fewer - The results some teams see: ~3x meetings booked and ~2x pipeline on the same headcount - Why "agents are easy to build" is a trap once you need shared data, governance, and calling/email infrastructure at scale - What stays human: judgment, narrative, and reading the room (the surf-small-talk story) -
